<a id="unified-dev-scorecard"></a>

## Dev leaderboard: all experiments

154 distinct saved systems; 100 dev queries; current corpus: 23,304 papers. **Working baseline: `fusion-shortlist+a=1+d=500`**. **Success score = nDCG@10**, descending using unrounded means; exact ties use stable system ID. Only fully judged runs with defined nDCG receive positions. The baseline stays at its actual position, not pinned first. Provisional runs appear separately, unranked. A leaderboard lead is not automatic baseline promotion.

**Technique guide:** Embedding identifies the vector model; Ranker / fusion identifies how retrieval results are ordered, not a separate LLM reranker. Tuned BM25 means exact terms + stems, authors, title x2, k1=0.8, b=0.75, no stopword removal. RRF uses reciprocal ranks; score fusion combines normalized BM25/cosine values. Depth is candidates per retriever, not final results. Frozen aliases can represent identical rankings under different experiment IDs. Readable names are presentation only: original IDs and files are preserved below.

All graded scores are recomputed from the **same immutable `score-fusion-dev/labels.json`**, including its 100 frozen human overrides. **Revised shared ideal-DCG denominator:** approved additive expansion preserves all 3190 original labels and adds 104 labels. Every system is rescored against this expanded denominator; original reports remain unchanged and their nDCG values must not be mixed with these revised scores. Other report scores/label pools and later judge-cache or workbook changes are NOT combined. Linear-gain nDCG@10 uses that shared ideal DCG; undefined queries are excluded only from nDCG (n shown). P@10 counts grades ≥1 with denominator 10. Unjudged gains count as zero. judged@10 is the judged fraction of returned results; short/missing lists still fail the full top-10 coverage gate.

**PROVISIONAL** means a dev top-10 position is missing or unjudged: source-paper MRR/recall remain valid on the full dev denominator (missing queries score zero), but graded scores are lower-bound diagnostics, not winner evidence. Paired nDCG against the CURRENT working baseline is withheld unless BOTH runs have every dev top-10 position judged. Intervals are exploratory query bootstraps conditional on these labels, not judge accuracy; no multiple-testing correction or test-query scoring. Known-item MRR is source-paper MRR on that type only.

**Snapshot/corpus caveat:** these are saved rankings, not fresh retrieval. Current corpus and dev-query fingerprints, the frozen label SHA256, ranking fingerprints, and all duplicate paths are recorded in the machine report. Older runs may not record a corpus fingerprint; matching paper IDs cannot prove identical build snapshots. Reduced-corpus embedding pilots are a separate scope, never scorecard rows. Costs/latencies are not estimated or assigned zero: only actually saved `.info.json` metadata is preserved per system, with its original timing scope. Historical reports retain their original labels, denominators, and controls.

## Historical source-paper experiment tables (original BM25 control)

The tables below retain their original saved scores and controls; use the unified scorecard above for comparisons against the current working baseline.

Each row is one search system, best first. Scores are against each query's source paper:
**R@k** = share of queries whose source paper is in the top k; **MRR@10** = average of
1 ÷ its rank (0 if below 10), with a 95% interval. **Δ vs baseline** is the paired
difference from `bm25-baseline` on the same queries: if its interval excludes 0, the
difference is real. The columns *keyword* to *broad* are MRR@10 within that group (dev:
25 per type, 74 specific, 26 broad). Broad queries have many right answers, so their
scores are a lower bound until the LLM judge grades other papers (nDCG@10 comes then).

**Careful:** picking the best of many rows on 100 dev queries flatters the winner a
little (winner's curse). The honest score is the finalist's run on test.

## Cached OpenAI fusion experiments

# Offline fusion dev experiment

Fixed baseline: `baseline-original-equal-rrf-c10-d100` (saved original equal RRF, c=10, depth=100).
Judge: `openai-mini`; rubric `b8b0c14a`; 3190/3190 pooled top-10 pairs judged; 100 human overrides.

**COMPLETE**

All systems use the same pooled labels plus human overrides for ideal DCG. Original graded.SYSTEMS top-10s remain in the pool. Unjudged gains are zero; nDCG with no positive labels is undefined. Source-paper metrics are separate. Candidate outputs contain up to 100 papers; a depth-20 union can be shorter.

Exploratory dev results, not held-out confirmation; no reranker. Judge calibration used one person's pilot labels, not independent validation. Paired 95% intervals are query-bootstrap intervals conditional on these labels, without multiple-comparison correction. Deltas are candidate minus fixed baseline.

## Score-fusion experiments (historical snapshot)

# Score-based fusion and deeper retrieval (dev only)

Cached embeddings; no baseline promotion. Judge calls this invocation: 0. All source top100 rankings exactly reproduce the frozen experiment. Cosine/BM25 scores are recomputed from cached vectors and the same lexical recipe.
max divides each list by its maximum; minmax subtracts its top-depth minimum then divides by its range. Each input is truncated to depth before normalization. Missing-list scores are zero. Constant positive lists receive unit scores.
Score weights are not comparable numerically to RRF weights. Top1 bonuses are fractions of each retriever's weighted rank-one RRF contribution.
**Incomplete graded scores are PROVISIONAL, not winner evidence.** All graded rows use one additive shared label snapshot; original grades are preserved and new cached judgments extend the ideal denominator. Unjudged gains count as zero. Source metrics are complete and remain valid. Label only missing pairs before comparing provisional graded results. Exploratory dev results and intervals are not multiple-testing adjusted.

New unjudged query-paper pairs across this grid: 0.

## Decision

Retain working baseline; keep scored fusion as challenger pending recall tradeoff approval.
Improved mean nDCG/MRR and first-place hits do not erase source recall regressions. Review all lost hits and lower-list relevance losses rather than treating leaderboard position as automatic promotion. Known-item target ranks are checked independently; the held-out test remains untouched.
Full abstracts, per-paper grades, raw normalized score contributions and ranks are in cases.json. All 100 query changes and segment CIs are in report.json.


## Rank/score interpolation experiments

# Rank/score interpolation: bounded dev experiment

Interpolating rank evidence with max-score fusion reduces weak-overlap boosting while retaining graded-relevance gains.

6 prespecified settings, depths100/500. Rank evidence is fixed RRF55%/c30/depth100 divided by1/31; score evidence is max-normalized75% semantic. Combined = a*score + (1-a)*normalized_RRF. These are not probabilities. No query-type routing, source IDs, or labels are used in ranking. Interpolation reranks the union of rank and score candidates.

Controls exactly reproduce frozen runs. All rows use the same parent snapshot. Paired graded comparisons are withheld for incomplete top10s; source metrics remain valid. Intervals are exploratory after dev tuning, not adjusted for selection or multiple testing. No automatic promotion or API calls.

## Fixed-shortlist score-ordering experiments

# Fixed-shortlist score ordering: bounded dev experiment

Score evidence improves ordering within the baseline top10 without sacrificing recall at10/20; MRR and known-item rank safety remain empirical.

4 prespecified settings, depths100/500. Rank evidence is fixed RRF55%/c30/depth100 divided by1/31; score evidence is max-normalized75% semantic. Combined = a*score + (1-a)*normalized_RRF. These are not probabilities. No query-type routing, source IDs, or labels are used in ranking. Shortlist mode only reorders baseline top10 and preserves the tail; it cannot introduce a paper or improve recall at10/20.

Controls exactly reproduce frozen runs. All rows use the same parent snapshot. Paired graded comparisons are withheld for incomplete top10s; source metrics remain valid. Intervals are exploratory after dev tuning, not adjusted for selection or multiple testing. No automatic promotion or API calls.

MS MARCO passage ranker, not specifically fine-tuned here for scientific abstracts or these dev queries. CPU float32, 512 tokens per query/document pair, preserve query and truncate document only. Scores are raw logits, not calibrated probabilities.

Frozen baseline: `fusion-shortlist+a=1+d=500`. Five settings fixed before outcomes; no promotion. Baseline-prefix depth10 isolates ordering; depth30/100 and union100 can replace the top10. Union100 is each retriever's top100, plus baseline100. 50/50 blend uses RRF c30, not averaged logits and cosine scores.

## Reproducibility

- `preregistration.json` and `input-provenance.json` freeze settings and inputs.
- Per-query `score-cache` files validate query/text/model fingerprints and complete candidate membership. Delete a specific damaged cache only deliberately; mismatches fail.
- Repeated runs reuse cached logits; no remote inference, paid embeddings or judging.
- `report.json`: paired bootstrap intervals, coverage, screening and per-query metrics.
- `cases.json`: source-rank wins/losses and top10 paper evidence, with missing grades explicit.
- Wall time includes tokenization and CPU inference, excludes model loading; it is an offline throughput measurement, not production request latency or a GPU benchmark.
- Broad-query source recall is only a single-target proxy. Dev intervals are exploratory; held-out test and human overrides remain untouched.


## Title/abstract field-score experiments

# Fixed-candidate field score experiment

Dev only; body = abstract. Frozen labels and human overrides unchanged. No paid calls or heldout evaluation. No promotion.

Seven prespecified configurations; all reorder exactly the Decision36 top100. Score = 75% baseline reciprocal rank (31/(30+r)) + 25% field evidence. Lexical: full-corpus independent BM25 exact+stems k1=.8/b=.75, candidate-max normalization; 10% author + 90% weighted title/abstract. Semantic: same local GTE model for concat and separate fields, normalized cosine mapped to [0,1].

Model: `thenlper/gte-small` revision `17e1f347d17fe144873b1201da91788898c639cd`; CPU float32, <=4 torch threads.

## Interpretation boundary

The semantic comparison tests a conservative 25% additional signal, not pure semantic ranking or retriever recall. Inspect top10-order-change counts before interpreting equal metrics: an unchanged top10 is no observable intervention at the primary cutoff, not evidence that separate field representations are useless. Same-model concat comparisons are recorded separately in report.json.

Follow-up to conservative field-score-dev semantic top10 no-op; remove base-rank dominance. Post-outcome exploratory, not confirmatory.

Sort Decision36 top10 by descending field signal only; stable baseline ties; preserve tail exactly. No query/label-dependent routing.

Concat: (cos(q,title+space+abstract)+1)/2; separate: (t*cos(q,title)+(1-t)*cos(q,abstract)+1)/2
